newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan may intervene if forex deviates too far - MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan may intervene if forex deviates too far - MOF.

text.p: Intervention in foreign exchange markets by Japanese authorities is possible if exchange rates deviate greatly from economic fundamentals, senior Ministry of Finance (MOF) official Eisuke Sakakibara said on Thursday.
Sakakibara, head of the ministry's International Finance Bureau, did not elaborate on whether Japan would intervene now but said recent dollar/yen movements were not in line with fundamentals.
"We do not think (dollar/yen movements) are in line with economic fundamentals. (The movements) are clearly too rapid."
Sakakibara said the Group of Seven (G7) nations agreed at their February meeting in Berlin that exchange rates should reflect fundamentals, and should move in a stable manner and not excessively.
"We are concerned (recent movements) have become too excessive," he said.
Asked whether the United States took the same view, Sakakibara said he could not comment on U.S. authorities' views, but added that Japan was keeping in close touch with them.

Sakakibara explained that comments by Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka earlier on Thursday that Japan would deal decisively with excessive currency movements meant that Japan would take "decisive action at an appropriate time".

On the Japanese economy, Sakakibara said market participants had become overly pessimistic about the outlook for the economy, and added that he believed this was reflected in a recent fall in Japanese long-term interest rates.
"If long-term interest rates do indeed reflect this excessive pessimism (the present level of long-term interest rates) will not be sustained for long," he said.
Sakakibara said recent economic indicators in Japan had been rather strong and said the market was taken up by "irrational negative exuberance".
He added: "The markets have become excessively pessimistic and this may turn out to be a disturbing factor within the markets in the future."

Asked whether foreign exchange rates would be discussed at a meeting between Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto and President Bill Clinton in late April, Sakakibara said he did not know whether foreign exchange rates would be discussed specifically, but added that it was possible for the issue to be included in talks on the economies of both nations.
